phylogenetic methods can be improved by adding incomplete taxa, even those with 50% of their data missing.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phylogenetic analyses of few taxa may often be rescued by adding taxa with a high level of missing data, and that this is true for all three of the most commonly-used phylogenetic methods.
adding taxa with missing data is better than adding characters, but adding characters with missing data is also better than adding taxa with missing characters.
phylogenies are essential in biology, but phylogeny estimation methods may give incorrect results under some conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best solution to the problem of limited taxon sample size is to increase taxon sample size.
the best solution in cases where limited taxon sampling leads to inaccurate estimates is to add more taxa, even if these taxa are highly incomplete.
the best strategy for resolving difficult phylogenetic questions is to sample as many complete taxa as possible (i.e., taxa that have data for all characters in all terminals).

phylogenetic analyses can be rescued from the negative impacts caused by limited taxon samples by adding taxa that are not only highly incomplete but also phylogenetically distant from the taxa already sampled.
